t: Morning, Gus. Day three of the rain. You'd love this.
Coo.
(quietly) You never finished your sentence. It's going to r... what? Rain? Run? Rhubarb?
Zero! Effie built a thing! It's loud, it's shiny, and I'm not allowed to touch it.
This is the Rewinder. Gus sees things backwards. So we are going to go backwards.
Back to the night of the freeze. We hear the rest of his sentence. Then we know how to fix him.
(from the doorway) Time travel. On a school night. ...I will allow it. It is educational.
One rule. The Rewinder only rides straight lines on the Time Grid. Every moment is a point.
Set the dial to the slope between two moments, and it rides the line. Get the slope wrong, and...
We explode?
We land somewhere else. Usually somewhere wet.
A practice jump first. We are here. Now.
Target: yesterday's lunch. A short hop.
Now is one across, two up. Lunch is four across, eight up.
Easy. Across three, up six. Three over six. One half! Set the dial to one half!
(waist-deep in the duck pond) Why is it ALWAYS the duck pond?
You put the climb on the bottom. One half is a very lazy slope.
Rise over run. How far UP goes on top. How far ACROSS goes underneath.
From now to lunch: up six, across three.
Six over three. The slope is two. Two up for every one across.
(dripping) Fine. Up first. Then across. Write it on my helmet.
Yesterday's lunch! There's me! And there's the last pudding!
(to his past self) Don't eat it! Save it for later! ...He can't hear me. He's eating it.
The past is read-only. We can watch. We can listen. We cannot touch.
Then we listen. Further back. All the way to the night of the freeze.
The trail keeps going along the same line. Last week is further up it.
A bigger jump. Five across. Ten up.
Ten over five. ...Two again?
Little stair, middle stair, big stair. Same shape, just grown.
Two over one. Six over three. Ten over five. Any two points on a straight line give the same slope.
Good evening. Day three of the rain. The forecast still says zero percent.
We have a caller.
(on the phone) Chip! It's Marcus. I'm calling from yesterday.
...And how is the weather in yesterday?
(on the phone) Dry. Also, somebody ate my pudding.
Caller, that was you. You ate it. I was there.
(on the phone) Spoilers, Chip!
Now we ride the other way. Back down the line, to the old bridge.
Going back means going down eight, and back four.
Minus eight over minus four? That's two minuses. That's double bad!
A minus over a minus is a plus. It's still two.
(quietly) Gus said it. Same line, either way you walk it.
Another trail! Twelve up at the start! That one looks way faster!
Read it left to right. Does it climb, or does it fall?
It falls. Down twelve, over six across.
Downhill is negative. Minus twelve over six. Minus two.
Ours climbs two. That one falls two. It's the Undefined's trail. We stay on ours.
The last jump. The Rewinder's log gives two marks on the line. No picture this time.
The bridge is two across, four up. The night of the freeze is seven across, fourteen up.
I've got this! Four take fourteen is minus ten. Seven take two is five. Minus two! Lever!
(chest-deep) Where are we?!
(reading the sign) Tomorrow. It's still raining. It's raining MORE.
You took them in different orders. Top: first minus second. Bottom: second minus first.
Same order, top and bottom. Fourteen take four is ten. Seven take two is five. Ten over five.
Two. The same line we've been riding all along.
So the minus sign wasn't double bad. It was just... in the wrong place.
(whispering) Gus. It's us. We came back for you.
He can't hear us. This moment is already written. Listen.
An r. Just an r. Then the line runs out.
The Undefined took the ground here. There's nothing left to ride on.
A slope tells us how steep the line is. It doesn't tell us where the line is.
Then we draw the whole line ourselves. Where it starts, and how it steps.

board: the same between ANY two points

t: (to frozen Gus) We heard an r, buddy. That's a start.
Coo.
Does finding an r count as a sidekick mission?
No.
